name: Equity dilution

subjectOf.text: The conversion feature of contingent convertible bonds affects corporate governance in a SIFI only if issuance volumes are sufficient and design features are adequate, because the governance effect runs through the threat of dilution of existing equity positions.
subjectOf.abstract: If sufficient volumes of contingent convertible bond issuances are combined with adequate design features, the conversion feature of contingent convertible bonds and the threat of dilution of equity positions in SIFIs could affect corporate governance in SIFIs.108
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Contingent Capital in Executive Compensation (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2097160
scope_conditions: sufficient volume of contingent convertible bond issuance

subjectOf.text: Contingent convertible bonds issued to executives are typically too small in volume to dilute investors' equity holdings or to supply a meaningful equity infusion during a crisis, so copying investor CoCo designs for executive pay produces suboptimal outcomes.
subjectOf.abstract: contingent convertible bonds may be issued to executives in volumes that may not suffice to dilute investors' equity holdings. The lower volume of contingent convertible bonds issued to executives may not provide a sufficiently strong equity infusion during a crisis.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Contingent Capital in Executive Compensation (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2097160
scope_conditions: contingent convertible bonds issued only to executives

subjectOf.text: The impending threat of dilution from a possible conversion of investor-held contingent convertible bonds can motivate existing shareholders to become actively involved in the governance of the entity.
subjectOf.abstract: The impending threat of dilution for existing shareholders due to the possible conversion of the contingent convertible bonds held by investors may motivate existing shareholders to get actively involved in the governance of the entity.181
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Contingent Capital in Executive Compensation (2012). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2097160
scope_conditions: investors also hold contingent convertible bonds subject to a later trigger

subjectOf.text: ICOs are preferable to venture capital funding for many start-ups first and foremost because ICO promoters and their developers are not forced to sacrifice equity in the project in exchange for the funds they raise.
subjectOf.abstract: First and foremost, ICO promoters and their developers are not forced to sacrifice their equity in the project in exchange for the funds they raised.36
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Marco Dell'Erba, Initial Coin Offerings Emerging Practices, Risk Factors, and Red Flags (2017). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3067615
scope_conditions: start-ups choosing between ICO and venture capital financing

subjectOf.text: Unlike other means of capital formation, ICOs allow promoters to raise funds without sacrificing equity, so proceeds can be used exclusively for product development.
subjectOf.abstract: Unlike other means of capital formation, ICO's allow promoters to avoid sacrificing equity for financing. Instead, ICO promoters can use the proceeds of the ICO exclusively for product development.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Initial Coin Offerings The Top 25 Jurisdictions and Their Comparative Regulatory Responses (2018). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3117224
